name: record_hypothesis
arguments: {"statement": "R28H removes a basic side-chain contact in the PH-domain inositol-phosphate pocket, so the PH domain binds Ins(1,3,4,5)P4 and related inositol phosphates less well and BTK is less efficiently recruited to the membrane.", "mechanism_class": "ligand_binding", "supports": ["E6", "E7", "E9", "E11", "E17", "E10"], "would_refute": "The R28 side chain lies more than about 4 \u00c5 from any atom of the bound 4IP ligand in 1B55, and an IP4 or IP6 binding measurement shows R28H binding at wild-type-like affinity.", "starting_rank": 1, "rank_rationale": "This is the only mechanism with direct residue-level support. UniProt annotates residue 28 as an inositol-phosphate binding site (E6). The 1996 binding assay reports a large IP4 binding loss for R28H (E7). The PH-domain structure places XLA mutations at the basic IP-binding end (E9). The 2013 MD study classifies R28H as functional rather than folding (E11), and 1B55 has 4IP bound at this residue (E17). Missing: a direct R28H binding measurement, and a check of the 1B55 contact distance (G1, G3)."}

arguments: {"statement": "R28H destabilises the PH-domain \u03b2-sandwich, so the domain folds less stably and is more prone to misfolding or degradation, which lowers the functional BTK pool regardless of ligand binding.", "mechanism_class": "stability_folding", "supports": ["E8", "E10", "E12", "E14", "E5"], "would_refute": "Stability calculations (for example FoldX or Rosetta \u0394\u0394G) give |\u0394\u0394G| below about 1 kcal/mol for R28H, and R28 is solvent-exposed in the AlphaFold model with no buried hydrogen-bond partner; the R28C structure 6TT2 at 1.36 \u00c5 also shows the wild-type fold.</refute>\n<parameter name=\"starting_rank\">2", "rank_rationale": "The support is indirect. Residue 28 sits in the PH domain and in a \u03b2-strand (E8, E5). Conservation is high (E12), and popEVE is strongly deleterious (E14), which could reflect folding as well as function. Missing: a \u0394\u0394G estimate or a stability measurement for R28H (G2)."}
